groups.text: It is currently 22 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

In Pakistan, the absence of a modern civic uprising mirrors a shift in how national narratives are formed compared to the Lawyers’ Movement of 2007 to 2009. That historical movement began as a dispute over the suspension of the chief justice but evolved into a nationwide campaign against General Musharraf's rule to restore the Constitution and democratic governance. While lawyers, judges, and political parties were central, the movement succeeded by using private television channels to transform a constitutional dispute into a mass mobilization. In unrelated technical news, developers have fixed an accuracy failure affecting Intel XPU hardware. The issue stemmed from the mm_plus_mm Triton template using descending loops, which caused the Triton-to-SPIR-V backend to miscompile negative-step loops. By converting these to ascending style loops, engineers validated a fix on the Intel Arc Pro B60, ensuring that previously failing 512x512 test cases now pass.

European nations are increasing their intake of Russian liquefied natural gas just as a total import ban looms for January 2027. According to the NGO Urgewald, EU countries paid an estimated 5.96 billion euros for Yamal LNG cargoes between January and June of this year. Most of these shipments arrived in Spain, Belgium, and France. The Yamal plant on Russia's Arctic peninsula is a critical asset, accounting for over 60 percent of Russia's total LNG exports. In the first half of 2026, European ports received 136 of the 140 cargoes shipped from the site. This represents a volume increase of 16 percent compared to the same period last year. These purchases boost Moscow's revenue amid escalating strikes against Ukraine, while Russia's ally China took only four cargoes during that same window. The EU remains Kyiv's primary wartime backer even as it funds this energy sector.

The plague remains as deadly today as it was during the Middle Ages, though it is now rare. The disease is caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis, which can damage various organs and cause bleeding. Without treatment, the infection leads to death in nearly one hundred percent of cases. In Oregon, a man named Paul Gaylord nearly died after being bitten by his sick cat. He initially received antibiotics for cat-scratch disease, but those medications failed because he actually had the plague. His condition worsened until he fell into a coma and required intensive care. While the illness still exists in places like Madagascar and the United States, experts say we do not need to fear a new pandemic. The primary danger today lies in the fact that symptoms are often non-specific, making it difficult for doctors to identify the infection quickly.

Chicago is effectively gaining its first ocean-served container terminal as Ports of Indiana-Burns Harbor prepares to open a new sea cargo box facility this year. Located in Portage, Indiana, about 20 miles from Chicago, the terminal will serve as the only all-water container gateway for the Greater Chicago market via the Great Lakes and St Lawrence Seaway. This project is part of a 100 million dollar expansion, the largest since the port opened in 1970, and includes new dock and rail infrastructure. The facility features 24-hour security and can connect directly with Europe or transship through Canadian ports, with a trial shipment planned before year's end. Meanwhile, in France, online service providers face a July 14 deadline to comply with CNIL regulations regarding tracking pixels in emails. Following a recommendation from March, companies must now obtain user consent before using these pixels, similar to marketing cookie rules. This has triggered a wave of information emails to users from banks and e-commerce sites.

Maritime security is collapsing in two critical corridors as commercial shipping comes under direct fire. In the Strait of Hormuz, a 7,000 teu container vessel operated by Global Feeder Shipping caught fire after an attack over the weekend, leaving one seafarer missing and triggering a wave of US and Iranian strikes across the region. The US has targeted Iranian missile systems and drone sites, while Iran has responded with attacks against Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, and Jordan. Meanwhile, Russia has suspended shipping through the Sea of Azov after Ukrainian drones hit ten tankers and four ferries in less than a week. This shutdown extends to the Don-Azov canal, disrupting Moscow's ability to move oil, grain, and military supplies. Amidst these geopolitical risks, Jiangnan Shipyard is proposing a radical shift in infrastructure with a concept for a floating, nuclear-powered logistics hub. The modular platform would act as an offshore container terminal and green-fuel factory to bypass coastal congestion and decarbonize trade.

Ukraine's Western allies are meeting in Paris today to increase pressure on Russia and reaffirm their support for Kyiv. President Volodymyr Zelensky will join at least 25 other leaders in a gathering of the Coalition of the Willing, where they will focus on air and missile defense cooperation. This urgency follows Saturday's Russian missile and drone attacks that killed eight people, leaving Ukraine exposed despite recent battlefield momentum. The group aims to secure more air-defense commitments and establish security guarantees for any eventual peace deal. In a separate matter of European policy, the Council of the European Union is expected to formally approve a package of reforms granting additional rights to air passengers today. These rules, already greenlighted by the European Parliament, will make compensation claims easier and ensure children under 14 can sit with parents without paying reservation fees.

The Ukrainian news outlet Ukrainska Pravda has received the Ischia Prize for achievements in European journalism. The award is granted under the patronage of the President of the Italian Republic, with winners selected by a dedicated jury. Representing the editorial team to receive the honor were editor-in-chief Sevgil Musayeva and Mykhailo Tkach, who leads the publication's investigative journalism department. This recognition highlights the outlet's role in reporting within the European media landscape.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 25 and 28 degrees and rain chances up to 18 percent.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the Berlin summer holidays all day, followed by the BLISS Reading Group at six forty-five in the evening and Twerchhau at seven in the evening.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
